purpose: Define propagation of origin identity/assurance context to remote governed resources while requiring the remote instance to evaluate its own AccessCore policy and preventing delegated rights expansion.

topics.name: Remote Authorization Propagation
topics.purpose: Define propagation of origin identity/assurance context to remote governed resources while requiring the remote instance to evaluate its own AccessCore policy and preventing delegated rights expansion.

semantics.origin_rule: Remote request carries exact origin identity/session/assurance provenance according to protocol policy.
semantics.remote_rule: Remote target evaluates its own AccessCore authorization policy.
semantics.nonexpansion_rule: Delegated remote path cannot expand rights beyond explicit delegation.
semantics.local_rule: A local owner may hold broader local rights where local policy permits; this does not imply those rights remotely.
semantics.dwh_rule: With AccessCore active, governed DWH remote access uses the DWH remote path rather than direct `$EXT` dereference.
semantics.assurance_rule: Remote target may impose its own minimum assurance requirement.
semantics.transport_rule: Secure transport/peer reachability does not grant remote authorization.
semantics.trace_rule: Remote decision retains origin identity plus remote policy/rule evidence.

invariants.rule: AccessCore activation, login, assurance and runtime protection are explicit lifecycle semantics; once active, AccessCore cannot be silently bypassed or disabled by an ungoverned runtime/config mutation.

hard_gates.condition: origin local rights copied wholesale to remote target
secure transport treated as remote authorization
direct $EXT bypasses governed DWH path under AC
remote target skips its own policy

references.purpose: AC-active remote DWH uses governed > addressing.

prose.summary: Define propagation of origin identity/assurance context to remote governed resources while requiring the remote instance to evaluate its own AccessCore policy and preventing delegated rights expansion.
